subject: Background of images are black not white

messages.author: 9994fc4e501f1f1a
messages.subject: Background of images are black not white
parts:
Hi Kyle,

First off I want to say thank you for such an amazing R package. It has been a life saver! I will definitely be getting good use out of it! 

It took me a little while to self-teach R, but when I found Cardinal I was super excited. 

When creating heat map images [image(data, mz=#)] the background shows up as black (See attached image - tad19.jpeg). In all of the examples I have seen of yours they are white.


Visually this isn't too bad, however when I attempt to perform PCA or spatial segmentation the "background" is being segmented as well, instead of only the spectra belonging to the tissue. 

I did a quick dig and I see that the pixels that are outside of the tissue have a "0" spectra (See  attached image - Spectra.jpeg). I'm thinking the problem is that the spectra have an intensity value of 0 for all m/z values rather than being "empty". 

Am I on the right track? Is there something that I can do to fix this? 

Other info: Data was acquired on a Bruker apexQe FTMS and exported to Analyze 7.5 format with FlexImaging 2.1. 

Script that was run: 
tad19name <- "tad19"

tad19folder <- "folder on my computer"

tad19_1 <- readAnalyze(tad19name, tad19folder)

> plot(tad19_1, pixel=100, main="pixel 100")

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Background of images are black not white
parts:
You're correct, Teesha. Your dataset currently includes the background pixels, and you want to crop them out.

You can do that using the "select" method, which plots an ion image while allowing you to select a region of interest and assign it to a variable. You can then use it to subset the dataset.

For example:

mysample <- select(tad19_1, mz=1000) # select the border around your sample
tad19_1 <- tad19_1[,mysample] # subset the dataset to only include the selected region

-Kylie

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Background of images are black not white
parts:
An alternative if the spectra for all of the background pixels are exactly 0 would be to automate it to drop 0-spectra:

empty <- pixelApply(tad19_1, .fun=function(s) all(s == 0)) # get all pixels with all 0 intensities
tad19_1 <- tad19_1[,!empty] # subset to include only non-empty pixels

-Kylie

Hi Kyle,

I forgot to let you know that this worked perfectly! I used your "alternative" approach because I knew that these extra pixels were for sure empty. No data was acquired for them during the experiment, they were just exported as 0-spectra when creating the .img file.
